A Ground-First Machine

They lean on tempo — a 62% no-huddle rate (league ~11%) that inflates snap counts and everyone's volume.

The Offensive Blueprint

There's no bell-cow to bank on — the lead back sees just 50% of carries (league ~59%), a committee that caps any one back's ceiling and makes their rushing props matchup- and script-dependent.

They live in the shotgun (91% of snaps vs ~68%) — a spread, pass-oriented structure.

Jayden Daniels is a scramble threat — he takes off on 6.7% of dropbacks (nearly double the 3.3% norm), rushing production that both lifts his own yardage and siphons a few carries from the backfield.

Chig Okonkwo is a genuine centerpiece, not an afterthought — 18% of targets (league ~15%).

By the numbers it's an efficient unit — a 47% success rate (above the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they lean run-heavy, passing 42% of the time, funnelling touchdown equity to Jacory Croskey-Merritt. And with the TE commanding 18% of targets, Chig Okonkwo is a live red-zone option too.

Defense — The Run Comes Free

Soft against opposing WR1s — 68 rec yds/game (vs ~58). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 143 rushing and 233 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.81/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They leak WR1 receiving TDs (0.51/game vs ~0.38) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They leak TE touchdowns (0.35/game vs ~0.24) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

Broadly a leaky unit — 46% success rate allowed (vs ~44%); points come easy against them.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back Jacory Croskey-Merritt's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line; opposing TE anytime-TD is a repeatable angle.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
